question: Pipe P can fill (2)/(3) part of a tank in 16 hours, and pipe Q can fill (5)/(6) part of the same tank in 20 hours. Both P and Q were kept open for 2 hours, then both were closed. Pipe R alone was then opened and it emptied the water in the tank in 8 hours. Pipes P, Q and R together can fill the empty tank in:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Time for full tank: P = 16 × 3/2 = 24 hrs, Q = 20 × 6/5 = 24 hrs.

Let Total Work = LCM(24, 24) = 24 units ⇒ Efficiency: P = 1, Q = 1.

Tank filled in 2 hrs = (1 + 1) × 2 = 4 units.

R empties 4 units in 8 hrs ⇒ R efficiency = −4 ÷ 8 = −0.5 units/hr.

Combined efficiency (P + Q + R) = 1 + 1 − 0.5 = 1.5 units/hr.

Time taken together = 24 ÷ 1.5 = 16 hours.

**∴ The correct answer is 16 hours.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

⇒ Time taken by P to fill 2/3 part of the tank = 16 hours.

⇒ Time taken by P to fill the complete tank = 16 × 3/2 = 24 hours.

⇒ Time taken by Q to fill 5/6 part of the tank = 20 hours.

⇒ Time taken by Q to fill the complete tank = 20 × 6/5 = 24 hours.

**Total Work and Efficiency:**

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total work done by P and Q in 2 hours = 2 × (1 + 1) = 4 units.

⇒ Both P and Q are closed, and these 4 units of water are emptied by pipe R in 8 hours.

⇒ Efficiency of emptying pipe R = Work ÷ Time = −4 ÷ 8 = −0.5 units/hr.

⇒ Combined efficiency of P, Q and R together = 1 + 1 − 0.5 = 1.5 units/hr.

⇒ Time taken by P, Q and R to fill the empty tank = Total Work ÷ Combined Efficiency.

⇒ Time taken = 24 ÷ 1.5 = 16 hours.

**∴ The correct answer is 16 hours.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Pipes & Cisterns Concept

This concept operates identically to standard Time & Work. The total capacity of the tank is considered the total work (assumed as the LCM of all given times). However, unlike regular workers, emptying pipes drain the tank, which is represented mathematically as a negative efficiency.

Combined Efficiency Rule

When multiple pipes (both filling and emptying) are opened simultaneously, their net rate of filling or emptying is the direct algebraic sum of their individual efficiencies. A positive net efficiency means the tank is getting filled over time.

Total Work Formula

Total Time Taken = Total Capacity of Tank ÷ Net Combined Efficiency of all active pipes.
